proposals.before: In the first year of Datong he was posthumously honored as Grand Mentor, commissioner with full plenipotentiary powers, Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, commander-in-chief over military affairs in twelve provinces including Ji and Ding, and governor of Ding province.
proposals.after: In the first year of Datong he was posthumously honored as Grand Commandant, commissioner with full plenipotentiary powers, Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, commander-in-chief over military affairs in twelve provinces including Ji and Ding, and governor of Ding province.
proposals.reason: 太尉 is Grand Commandant (or Grand Marshal), not Grand Mentor (太傅).

proposals.before: In the first year of Datong he was posthumously awarded Grand Mentor, commissioner bearing the staff with full powers, Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, commander over the military affairs of the twelve provinces including Ji and Ding, and Governor of Ding Province.
proposals.after: In the first year of Datong he was posthumously awarded Grand Commandant, commissioner bearing the staff with full powers, Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, commander over the military affairs of the twelve provinces including Ji and Ding, and Governor of Ding Province.
proposals.reason: 太尉 is Grand Commandant, not Grand Mentor.

proposals.before: His grandfather Bofu distinguished himself in the late Taihe campaigns against Xuanchi and was appointed administrator of Runan commandery.
proposals.after: His grandfather Bofu distinguished himself in the late Taihe campaigns against Xuanhu and was appointed administrator of Runan commandery.
proposals.reason: 懸瓠 is Xuanhu (Xuánhú), not Xuanchi.

proposals.before: His grandfather Bofu, at the end of the Taihe era of Wei, followed the campaign against Xuanchi with merit and became Administrator of Runan Commandery.
proposals.after: His grandfather Bofu, at the end of the Taihe era of Wei, followed the campaign against Xuanhu with merit and became Administrator of Runan Commandery.
proposals.reason: 懸瓠 is Xuanhu, not Xuanchi.

proposals.before: [xian [in the received text]] duke, with a fief increased by one thousand households.
proposals.after: county duke, with a fief increased by one thousand households.
proposals.reason: Editorial bracket note left in idiomatic English; 縣公 should read as county duke continuing s0207.

proposals.before: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, his rank was advanced to earl, and his fief was increased to nine hundred households in all with what came before.
proposals.after: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, Xuan's rank was advanced to earl, and his fief was increased to nine hundred households in all with what came before.
proposals.reason: The pronoun 'his' after Emperor Xiaomin wrongly suggests the emperor was enfeoffed; the Chinese silent subject is Wei Xuan.

proposals.before: In the fourth year he was made General of Agile Cavalry with a baron's establishment equal to the Three Dukes and moved his garrison to Yanhan.
proposals.after: In the fourth year he was made General of Agile Cavalry and Equal to the Three Dukes with a Separate Office, and moved his garrison to Yanhan.
proposals.reason: 開府儀同三司 is the honorific Kaifu Yitong Sansi, not a baronial establishment; 'baron's establishment' mistranslates 開府.

proposals.before: In the fourth year he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry and Baron with an establishment equal to the Three Dukes, and transferred his garrison to Yanhan.
proposals.after: In the fourth year he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry and Equal to the Three Dukes with a Separate Office, and transferred his garrison to Yanhan.
proposals.reason: 開府儀同三司 does not mean 'Baron with an establishment'; it is the Kaifu Yitong Sansi honor.

proposals.before: [zhou [in the received text]] Commander-in-Chief Yuchi Gang sent Xuan with Yuwenneng, Zhao Gan, and five hundred foot and horse south of Lulu Crossing to ambush Dugu Yongye, Eastern Wei's governor of Luo province.
proposals.after: [zhou [in the received text]] Commander-in-Chief Yuchi Gang sent Xuan with Yitong Yuwen Neng, Zhao Gan, and five hundred foot and horse south of Lulu Crossing to ambush Dugu Yongye, Eastern Wei's governor of Luo province.
proposals.reason: 儀同宇文能 is the officer Yuwen Neng holding the Yitong rank; 'Yuwenneng' fuses the surname and given name and omits the office title.

proposals.before: [zhou [in the received text]] Commander-in-Chief Yuchi Gang sent Xuan leading Yuwenneng, Baron with an establishment, Zhao Gan, and others with five hundred infantry and cavalry south of Lulu Crossing to intercept and strike Dugu Yongye, Eastern Wei's governor of Luo province.
proposals.after: [zhou [in the received text]] Commander-in-Chief Yuchi Gang sent Xuan leading Yitong Yuwen Neng, Zhao Gan, and others with five hundred infantry and cavalry south of Lulu Crossing to intercept and strike Dugu Yongye, Eastern Wei's governor of Luo province.
proposals.reason: 儀同 before 宇文能 is the Yitong honor/office, not 'Baron with an establishment', and the name should be spaced as Yuwen Neng.

proposals.before: By this they were able to display arms at the Yi and Luo, hold and secure Xiao and Han, make the men of Qi frustrate their plan of advancing west, and ease the Zhou court's concern of looking east—all through the power of these several generals.
proposals.after: By this they were able to display arms at the Yi and Luo, hold and secure Xiao and Han, frustrate the men of Qi in their plan of advancing west, and ease the Zhou court's concern of looking east—all through the power of these several generals.
proposals.reason: 齊人沮西略之謀 means Qi's western-expansion plan was frustrated, not that the men of Qi themselves frustrated their own plan.

decisions.reason: s0019 has 追贈太尉; 太尉 is Grand Commandant, whereas Grand Mentor is 太傅, so the replacement corrects a real title error.
Literal of s0019 likewise renders 太尉 wrongly as Grand Mentor; Grand Commandant matches the Chinese office.
s0003 has 從征懸瓠; 懸瓠 is the place Xuanhu, not Xuanchi, so the naming repair is required.
Literal of s0003 has the same 懸瓠; Xuanhu is the accurate English form and Xuanchi is wrong.
s0209 reads 〔縣〕公 after 許昌 in s0207; the idiomatic field wrongly keeps editorial apparatus instead of rendering 縣公 as county duke.
s0214's silent subject continues Wei Xuan's biography (進爵為伯); after 孝閔帝踐阼, bare 'his' wrongly suggests the emperor was enfeoffed, and naming Xuan matches the idiomatic field and context.
s0216 has 開府儀同三司, the Kaifu Yitong Sansi honor; 'baron's establishment' invents a noble fief reading of 開府 and must be replaced.
Literal of s0216 likewise mistranslates 開府儀同三司 as a baronial establishment; Equal to the Three Dukes with a Separate Office is the correct honorific.
s0220 has 儀同宇文能; 儀同 is the Yitong rank and 宇文能 is Yuwen Neng, so fused 'Yuwenneng' without the office is wrong.
Literal of s0220 wrongly turns 儀同 into 'Baron with an establishment' and fuses 宇文能; Yitong Yuwen Neng restores both office and name spacing.
s0199 has 齊人沮西略之謀; 沮 marks the Qi western plan as frustrated by the Zhou generals, not Qi men frustrating their own plan.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0009 shows English Yuwenneng came only from fusing 宇文能; the personal-name claim must use Yuwen Neng while keeping zh, pinyin, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
